workspace_rules.rule: Do not combine sqlx 0.9.x with rusqlite 0.41.x / sqlite-wasm-rs 0.6.x in one Cargo workspace: sqlx-sqlite bounds libsqlite3-sys <0.38 and Cargo enforces links="sqlite3" even for sqlx's optional sqlite backend. A shared workspace must use rusqlite 0.39.0 + sqlite-wasm-rs 0.5.5.
workspace_rules.verified: cargo generate-lockfile probe with all crates =latest failed; succeeded with rusqlite 0.39.0 + sqlite-wasm-rs 0.5.5
workspace_rules.removal_condition: sqlx (now transact-rs/sqlx) releases with a libsqlite3-sys bound that includes the version used by the latest rusqlite. No upstream issue found.

owner_constraints: No paid or proprietary products. The cache is an NDS Rust implementation or reuses open-source components written in Rust.
Clients reach the cache only over the internal network, and every client authenticates with a key.
Consumers are owner devices and private self-hosted GitHub Actions runners. Public repositories keep free GitHub-hosted runners.

rust_components.role: Rust/C/C++ compiler cache client with an S3-compatible backend

rust_components.name: RustFS
rust_components.role: S3-compatible object store for build-cache and blob storage; already used by company stacks

module_protocols.protocol: PyPI simple index and files (uv, pip)
crates.io sparse index and crate files

module_protocols.protocol: Go module proxy, checksum database and golang.org/toolchain

module_protocols.note: archive_url values are absolute and may be signed, so a plain reverse proxy does not cache archives (reported).

module_protocols.protocol: Maven repositories (Maven Central, Google Maven, Gradle Plugin Portal)
module_protocols.client: Gradle init script in ~/.gradle/init.d replacing repositories

module_protocols.protocol: OCI distribution pull-through (docker.io, ghcr.io, gcr.io, cgr.dev) and pushed BuildKit cache refs
module_protocols.client: Docker registry-mirrors for Docker Hub; containerd hosts.toml under /etc/docker/certs.d/<registry>/ for other registries; buildkitd.toml mirrors

module_protocols.upstream: static.rust-lang.org, storage.googleapis.com/flutter_infra_release, python-build-standalone releases, cdn.playwright.dev, services.gradle.org distributions, GitHub release assets
module_protocols.client: RUSTUP_DIST_SERVER and RUSTUP_UPDATE_ROOT; FLUTTER_STORAGE_BASE_URL; UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_MIRROR; PLAYWRIGHT_DOWNLOAD_HOST; Gradle distributionUrl with distributionSha256Sum; mise url_replacements and playbook-dev-devices artifact URLs
settings.gradle(.kts) buildCache remote HttpBuildCache; CI pushes, devices load only

constraints.fact: Docker registry-mirrors only mirror Docker Hub.
dockerd reads containerd hosts.toml from /etc/docker/certs.d/<registry>/ with the containerd image store.
Go toolchain auto-download goes through GOPROXY as module golang.org/toolchain and requires checksum database verification.
sccache Rust caching requires incremental compilation disabled and cannot cache bin, dylib, cdylib and proc-macro crates.
sccache cross-machine Rust hits need identical absolute paths.
sccache with bazel-remote does not work (open issue).
Develocity/Gradle Build Cache Node is deprecated and unavailable after 2026-12-31.
Android sdkmanager has HTTP/SOCKS proxy options but no mirror URL setting.
Several clients cannot send credentials to a mirror (rustup; likely Flutter storage and Playwright downloads).

build_caches.rust: Devices keep the managed per-device Cargo build-dir. A shared sccache on RustFS is limited to CI release builds; CI writes, devices read only.
build_caches.docker: BuildKit type=registry cache refs pushed only by CI identities.
build_caches.gradle: HTTP build cache served by the module; CI pushes, devices load only.
build_caches.c-cpp: ccache remote storage through storage helpers, read-only for devices (reported).

security: Serve only on the internal network with trusted TLS and per-client keys; clients that cannot send credentials are admitted by network identity only.
Shared build caches are writable only by CI identities; devices and pull-request jobs read only.
Untrusted pull-request code never receives cache write keys.
Private package names are never proxied to public upstreams.
